author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Bishop Rodríguez outlines efforts to protect vulnerable in Diocese of Palm Beach
text:
Bishop Manuel de Jesús Rodríguez said on April 29 that the Diocese of Palm Beach is committed to maintaining safe environments for children and vulnerable adults. He explained that his experience in adjudicating cases involving sexual abuse and misconduct has given him a detailed understanding of church norms for handling such offenses.
The topic is important as it highlights ongoing efforts by the Catholic Church to address abuse, particularly during National Child Abuse Prevention Month. The diocese aims to ensure safety in its parishes, schools, and other entities by implementing strict procedures and fostering a culture focused on protection.
“I have a very detailed idea of what the church has in place in its norms in terms of the treatment of offenses of sexual abuse and any kind of sexual misconduct that can affect minors, vulnerable persons or adults,” Bishop Rodríguez told the Florida Catholic. He added that he spent six years researching his doctoral dissertation on victims of sexual abuse in penal canonical cases, working with international experts including Jesuit Father Hans Zollner.
Bishop Rodríguez said his research compared current church norms with state laws from several countries. “What I did with that multiyear research was to engage in an examination of the current norms and processes and procedures in place to address matters of sexual abuse in the church and compare them with regular state laws” in countries such as the United States, France, Chile, and Nigeria.
Upon becoming leader of the diocese on Feb. 24, Bishop Rodríguez assumed responsibility for overseeing safe environment policies through the Office of Safe Environments. According to diocesan policy: “Recognizing that each individual is created by God, the Diocese of Palm Beach is committed to the safety and well-being of its children and vulnerable adults… The diocese does not tolerate abuse or neglect.”
“That’s our most important duty. Safeguarding the dignity and safety of everyone who takes part in any activity within the church,” he said. Bishop Rodríguez also stressed proactive prevention measures: “That means we are always proactive… standards… due diligence… prevention.”
He further noted that compliance administrators across diocesan entities play a key role by keeping records up-to-date regarding screening, training, code-of-conduct compliance for employees and volunteers. Regular workshops help maintain awareness among administrators about policies ahead of audits.
Annual independent audits review background checks for staff members as well as ongoing education programs designed to prevent abuse.
